outcomes.statement: A colleague can start a genuinely new software project under AES governance, move from accepted intent through planned realization and implementation to evidence-backed current/gap state, and do so without access to private historical repositories or undocumented AES lineage knowledge.

Real implementation work in an AES-governed repository lands only under a plan that Company Planning adopted; trivial work still lands, decided by measured facts about the change, not by the tag an agent types.

normative_items.statement: The supported AES distribution and its required dependencies must be obtainable and documented without access to Brian's private historical repositories.
Before governed implementation begins, AES must represent accepted normative obligations, success/disproof semantics, and what evidence is capable of establishing each exercised criterion.
Every durable governed repository artifact must be justified by an accepted exact planned path or a bounded accepted artifact-generation rule.

AES planning must derive accepted capability requirements, realization boundaries, durable repository topology, selected load-bearing symbol commitments where needed, and criterion-linked verification topology before governed execution of those commitments.

The working context for a governed subject must contain the full applicable normative, success and disproof meaning with provenance rather than requiring the acting agent to dereference identifiers before understanding its obligations.
AES must produce revision-bound structured characterization of the realized repository sufficient to compare accepted artifact and selected symbol/signature/type commitments with realized state.
Observation result, evidence freshness, evidence adequacy, qualified current, gap, and plan completion must remain semantically distinct.

AES must derive qualified current state and gap state from accepted target plus revision-bound realized observations and evidence assessments, preserving missing, stale, error, contradictory and insufficient-evidence conditions rather than rendering them green.
Greenfield-MVP acceptance must be established on a genuinely fresh consumer project governed by AES from inception; success on AES canonical's existing repository alone is insufficient.

v0.1 code is retained, not deleted. Phase 7a dispositioned it: the eight empty v0.1 component placeholders were moved with history to archive/v0.1-placeholders/ (historical); repository_context/ (the installed console script aes-repo-context, tested by tests/repository_context/) and the package __init__.py are retained, each a planned artifact of this target so the no-orphan rule holds. They carry no v0.2 obligation; changing them is v0.1 maintenance, not v0.2 work.

Every commit message's first line carries one of [Plan #N], [Goal <id>], [Trivial], [Unplanned] or [Shaping <id>] (git's own merge, fixup and squash messages excepted), and the rule checks the tag against facts: an adopted receipt for the named plan, the staged diff's measured size and paths, an Emergency trailer, or the plan's proposals folder.

In a repository that requires adopted plans, a target change is accepted only for a proposal whose adopted_plan_ref names a Company Planning plan adopted for its current bytes; a proposal that names a plan is checked the same way in any repository.

Every proposal declares whether its work runs a model, agent or pipeline (trace_review); a proposal declaring traced work adds or changes a success criterion with an evidence requirement of kind trace_review; an observation assessing a trace_review requirement carries a TraceReview record whose reviewer is not the author, and may SUPPORT only when every trace step was read and no checked decision was wrong.
 Supporting standing additionally requires a fresh invocation of the configured Company Planning source-bound review provider against retained trace bytes, exact criterion/revision linkage and reviewer identity. Missing provider, partial coverage, altered bytes or fabricated citations leave standing insufficient; review completeness never changes a failed run verdict.

aes adopt writes .aes/legacy_baseline.json listing every tracked file under the governed roots at a named revision with its blob hash (minus files the target already plans), initializing the project first when it has no .aes/. Baseline files the target does not plan are legacy, not orphans, in topology, characterize and reconcile; a file in neither is still an orphan. A commit that modifies a legacy file is an unplanned legacy edit under the commit rule's mode (observe logs it, enforce refuses it), except Git's own messages and [Unplanned] emergencies. aes plan accept removes baseline entries the target now plans or Git no longer tracks. aes status shows the legacy share and how many legacy files changed since adoption.

success_criteria.statement: A fresh user with no access to Brian's other private repositories can install/configure the supported AES distribution and initialize a new governed project using only distributed material and declared dependencies.
success_criteria.disproof: Successful initialization requires copying undeclared files, private-repo access, or undocumented historical knowledge.

evidence_requirements.requirement: Validate the accepted target model for resolvable normative-to-criterion and criterion-to-evidence-requirement links.

success_criteria.statement: The accepted realization topology accounts for every durable governed artifact by exact path or bounded accepted generation rule and gives every artifact a semantic purpose.
success_criteria.disproof: A durable governed artifact can exist without an accepted exact path, applicable bounded generation rule, or semantic justification.

success_criteria.statement: A fresh implementing agent receives the complete applicable normative, success and disproof text with provenance in the bounded working context for the selected subject.

success_criteria.statement: At an exact revision AES characterizes the realized repository and mechanically detects missing/undeclared durable artifacts plus selected symbol/signature/type drift when such commitments exist.
success_criteria.disproof: Target-realized comparison requires manual reconstruction of repository contents or silently accepts an intentional drift.

evidence_requirements.requirement: Deliberately mutate one planned artifact or selected symbol commitment and observe a target-realized mismatch.

success_criteria.statement: A pass-like observation with insufficient required evidence does not render the associated criterion satisfied or its gap closed.
success_criteria.disproof: Any passing test automatically produces criterion satisfaction regardless of the criterion's evidence requirements.

evidence_requirements.requirement: Construct a criterion requiring multiple evidence inputs, provide only one passing observation, and verify adequacy remains INSUFFICIENT and standing is not promoted to supported closure.

success_criteria.statement: Material change to an evidence dependency invalidates or stales affected evidence/current state until applicable evidence is re-established.
success_criteria.disproof: A materially changed subject can retain green current/gap state solely because older evidence once passed.

evidence_requirements.requirement: Change one material dependency after successful verification and verify affected evidence/current becomes stale or otherwise non-current before re-verification.

success_criteria.statement: With the commit-message hook installed, a staged change adding a Dockerfile committed as "[Unplanned] ..." with no Emergency trailer is judged refuse and names the running-thing file; the same change under a [Goal <id>] whose plan is adopted is judged accept; a one-line README change under [Trivial] is judged accept; in observe mode every verdict is logged and none blocks.
success_criteria.disproof: The rule accepts or refuses on the tag text alone; or a running-thing file passes as [Trivial]; or a [Goal] or [Plan] commit is accepted with no adopted receipt, or with a receipt for older plan bytes; or observe mode blocks a commit.

success_criteria.statement: With require_adopted_plan true, `aes plan validate` and `aes plan accept` refuse a proposal with no adopted_plan_ref, one naming a missing plan, and one whose plan changed after adoption, each with the reason; the same proposal naming a freshly adopted plan is accepted. success_criteria.disproof: accept succeeds without an adopted receipt where one is required, or with a receipt for older plan bytes; or the default (setting absent) refuses a proposal that does not name a plan.

evidence_requirements.requirement: Tests run `aes plan validate` and `aes plan accept` in real Git repositories for each case above, asserting exit status, the reason text and whether the target and plan file were written.

"""AES canonical governs itself (roadmap phase 6b, `SC-GF-003`, `SC-GF-004`).

Unlike every other file in this directory, these tests read the live
repository they are part of, not a fixture or a temporary clone: the subject
is AES's own `.aes/` target at the checked-out revision. That is intended. The
repository governing itself is the claim, so the check has to run against it.

ER-SC-GF-003-02: the unchanged planned topology is accepted at HEAD (every
governed file, the retained v0.1 files included, is a planned artifact).
ER-SC-GF-004-01: every evidence requirement in the live target has a route.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from ruamel.yaml import YAML

from agentic_engineering_system.cli import main
from agentic_engineering_system.planning import route_violations
from agentic_engineering_system.records import load_project, load_target
from agentic_engineering_system.topology import compare_topology, normalized_roots

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
# The accepted copy (Decision 0010), not the proposal lineage file it was copied from.
SEMANTIC_INSTANCE = REPO / "docs" / "architecture" / "greenfield-v0.2" / "12-greenfield-mvp-semantic-instance.yaml"
V01_RETAINED = ("repository_context",)  # real v0.1 code: console script aes-repo-context
V01_ARCHIVED = (  # empty placeholders, moved to archive/v0.1-placeholders/ in phase 7a
    "capability_sourcing", "evidence_assessment", "execution", "gap_reconciliation", "learning",
    "normative_context", "planning", "policy_control",
)


def _target():
    project = load_project(REPO / ".aes" / "project.yaml")
    return project, load_target(REPO / project.materialization.target_path)


def _words(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(str(text).split())


def test_own_target_loads_strictly_with_the_greenfield_criteria_verbatim():
    _, target = _target()
    source = YAML(typ="safe").load(SEMANTIC_INSTANCE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    want = {c["id"]: c for c in source["success_criteria"]}
    # the greenfield criteria, verbatim; later outcomes (SC-AP-*, PLAN-AES-COMMIT-RULE) add their own
    got = {c.id: c for c in target.success_criteria if c.id.startswith("SC-GF-")}
    assert sorted(got) == sorted(want) == [f"SC-GF-00{i}" for i in range(1, 10)]
    for sc_id, c in want.items():
        assert _words(got[sc_id].statement) == _words(c["statement"]), sc_id
        assert _words(got[sc_id].disproof) == _words(c["disproof"]), sc_id
        assert got[sc_id].target_refs == c["target_refs"], sc_id
        assert [(e.id, _words(e.requirement)) for e in got[sc_id].evidence_requirements] == [
            (e["id"], _words(e["requirement"])) for e in c["evidence_requirements"]
        ], sc_id
    items = {n.id: n for n in target.normative_items}
    for n in source["normative_items"]:
        assert _words(items[n["id"]].statement) == _words(n["statement"]), n["id"]


def test_topology_at_head_has_no_orphan_and_plans_the_v01_files_as_history():
    project, target = _target()
    governed = normalized_roots(project.governed_roots)
    listed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "-z", "HEAD", "--", *governed],
        cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    ).stdout
    files = tuple(p for p in listed.split("\0") if p)
    report = compare_topology(governed, files, target)
    assert report.orphans == ()
    by_path = {a.locator.exact_path: a for a in target.planned_artifacts}
    v01 = [p for p in files if p.split("/")[2] in V01_RETAINED]
    assert v01 and "src/agentic_engineering_system/repository_context/cli.py" in v01
    for path in [*v01, "src/agentic_engineering_system/__init__.py"]:
        assert by_path[path].semantic_justification_refs == ["NI-AES-HIST"], path
    # the archived placeholders left the governed root and the target, and kept their history
    gone = tuple(f"src/agentic_engineering_system/{pkg}/" for pkg in V01_ARCHIVED)
    assert not [p for p in [*files, *by_path] if p.startswith(gone)]
    archived = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "HEAD", "--", "archive/v0.1-placeholders/"],
        cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    ).stdout.split()
    assert sorted(archived) == sorted(
        [f"archive/v0.1-placeholders/{pkg}/component.placeholder.yaml" for pkg in V01_ARCHIVED]
        + ["archive/v0.1-placeholders/README.md"]
    )
    assert "tests/greenfield/test_self_governance.py" in by_path


def test_every_greenfield_evidence_requirement_has_a_route():
    _, target = _target()
    assert route_violations(target) == []
    external = {b.evidence_requirement_ref for b in target.external_boundaries}
    assert {e for e in external if e.startswith("ER-SC-GF-")} == {"ER-SC-GF-001-01", "ER-SC-GF-005-02", "ER-SC-GF-009-01"}
    assert external - {"ER-SC-GF-001-01", "ER-SC-GF-005-02", "ER-SC-GF-009-01"} == {"ER-AP-001-02"}


def test_aes_status_on_this_repository_exits_zero(capsys):
    assert main(["status", "--root", str(REPO)]) == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "agentic-engineering-system-canonical-target" in out
    assert "0 orphan(s)" in out
